image.title: DW
image.description: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

item.title: India: Delhi surpasses Lahore as world's most polluted city
item.description: Delhi's Air Quality Index (AQI) was recorded to be higher than Lahore in Pakistan on Friday, which made it the most polluted city globally.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Gen Z protests: Do Baby Boomers really have it better than young people?
item.description: Should young people in Germany be more worried about their future than Baby Boomers were in the 1980s and 1990s? Or should both generations take to the streets and protest together? DW checked the data.
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: Senegal Youth Olympics in Dakar end on high note
item.description: Enthusiastic crowds attended the games in Senegal, with China taking home the most gold medals. It's the first Olympic Games since Russia's war on Ukraine where Russian athletes can compete under their own flag.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Trump to meet Xi, Putin for three-way huddle on nuclear arms talks
item.description: The White House has said President Donald Trump will urge Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin to discuss cutting nuclear arsenals in Shenzhen next week, though a senior US official expects no agreement.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: SpaceX launches Starship rocket, fails to recover booster
item.description: SpaceX had planned to catch and later reuse both stages of its biggest rocket for the first time. But the booster exploded over the Gulf of Mexico, while the spacecraft continued into orbit.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: US lifts nationwide ground stop for airports hours after halting all departures
item.description: The US federal aviation regulator has lifted a nationwide ground stop for all airports. Trump administration officials blame "overloaded" and "outdated" systems for the hourslong halt to departures.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Tanker collides with cruise ship on Mississippi in New Orleans
item.description: A freighter collided with a cruise ship carrying around 130 people in New Orleans, causing the paddlewheel vessel to capsize. More than 30 people were hospitalized, but all passengers survived and were accounted for.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Ukraine updates: Europe to send united front to potential peace talks
item.description: Germany, France, the UK, Italy and Poland — as well as the EU itself — will jointly represent Europe in possible peace talks. Meanwhile, a second car bomb in two days has exploded in Moscow.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: David Walliams: UK police launch sex offense probe into comedian
item.description: The "Little Britain" star and "Britain's Got Talent" judge has been accused of engaging in sexual misconduct and inappropriate behavior towards young women and girls. Walliams denies the allegations.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Pope Leo celebrates Mass in his former diocese of Chiclayo, Peru
item.description: Over a million people have gathered for Mass with Pope Leo XIV on Friday. The event in northern Peru, where he served as bishop before becoming head of the Catholic Church, is the centerpiece of his South American tour.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: The dangers of revising Europe's security architecture
item.description: Experts warn against revising Europe's security framework because they say it would mean granting Moscow its longstanding wish of renegotiating postwar security on the continent.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: EU leaders urged to 'act now' to stay AI competitive with US, China
item.description: EU leaders in Dublin were called on by an AI executive to move quickly in the tech race with the US and China. EU official Metsola, however, expressed frustration with the idea that the bloc is behind in AI development.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: What's going on with the polar vortex?
item.description: Observations show the ring of fierce winds that rotate at the Earth's North Pole has changed direction. Scientists say it's a historic disruption and the earliest reversal on record. What could it mean for the weather?
item.dc:subject: Environment

item.title: Ice hockey: Russia threatens against Canada and Germany over exclusion from tournaments
item.description: A fortnight after the CAS ordered ice hockey's governing body to reintegrate Russia into international play, a solution remains elusive. Now Russia has threatened to take legal action against two tournament hosts.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Why does El Salvador's Bukele have troops in Haiti?
item.description: Haiti's Prime Minister congratulating El Salvador's President for a gang crackdown in Haiti has shone a light on the relationship between the two countries. What's going on, and where does the US stand?
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Iran targeted US radar system in Bahrain
item.description: Iran claimed it struck US radar systems in Bahrain, while the US said it had intercepted the attacks. Clashes continue in the Strait of Hormuz, as the war remains in a state of de-escalation.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Beijing faces its Russia dilemma amid talk of Xi-Trump-Putin summit
item.description: China is forced to tread carefully as it considers hosting a meeting between Xi Jinping, Vladimir Putin, and Donald Trump. While the optics are sure to favor Moscow, Beijing is risking its image at the global stage.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Cyber attacks and hybrid warfare: Germany gives sweeping powers to its police and intelligence services
item.description: Drone sightings and cyberattacks have heightened security concerns. How are the police preparing to meet these challenges? And how do intelligence services plan to counter threats from both domestic and foreign sources?
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: Indonesia's wiretapping scandal opens a political fault line
item.description: Senior police officers are accused of illegally monitoring President Prabowo Subianto, exposing rival networks within Indonesia's security establishment and renewing concerns about political misuse of surveillance.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Is the AI bubble bursting just as Anthropic goes public?
item.description: The sharp sell-off in tech stocks after the US midterms has cast doubt on Anthropic's looming IPO. Yet with hundreds of billions still being invested, some think the AI party is still in full swing.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Germany's Nmecha won't repeat controversial goal celebration
item.description: Germany head coach Jürgen Klopp says that midfielder Felix Nmecha will not repeat a goal celebration that sparked controversy over the past week. Germany are set to face Serbia and the Netherlands in the Nations League.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Germany news: Parliament agrees on debt-laden 2027 budget
item.description: The budget committee in the Bundestag worked into the night to sign off on next year's spending plans. These include levels of new debt only eclipsed once, at the height of the COVID pandemic. DW has more.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Czechia braces for massive protest against public media reform plans
item.description: A fast-tracked bill to cut public media funding has sparked strikes, rallies and fears for the independence of public broadcasting in Czechia. A massive protest is planned for Prague on Sunday.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Could lack of money sink TFFF rainforest fund before it even launches?
item.description: The TFFF rainforest fund aims to make forest conservation more profitable than deforestation. But a lack of money may prevent it from getting off the ground.
item.dc:subject: Environment

item.title: Iranian activist and Nobel Peace Prize winner Narges Mohammadi shares her story in memoir
item.description: Written and smuggled out of prison, the 2023 Nobel Prize laureate's memoir reveals the cost of defying Iran's regime and fighting for freedom.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: EU leaders tussle over whom to send to Ukraine, Russia peace talks
item.description: A seat at the table for Europe now appears likely following comments by a US envoy who just held talks with Putin. But who will take that seat remains unclear.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Can the EU make it harder to trick consumers online?
item.description: The EU wants to curb subscription traps, misleading sales tactics and features that keep people scrolling. What would the proposed Digital Fairness Act change, and does it go far enough?
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: What have the talks with Russia and the US in Abu Dhabi achieved for Ukraine?
item.description: The first trilateral talks between Ukraine, the US and Russia in nine months have ended with an agreement on exchanging prisoners. Does this mark a genuine breakthrough and a step toward peace?
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Hungary eases abortion restrictions in women's rights overhaul
item.description: The reforms mark a break the the conservative policies of former PM Viktor Orban. The controversial "heartbeat regulation" is to be scrapped and women are to be better protected against violence.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: UK court convicts 2 Iranian men of spying on journalists
item.description: A London court has found two Iranian citizens guilty of surveilling reporters for a Persian-language television station critical of Iran's government. One was also convicted of planning a violent attack against them.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Jensen Huang: Spy row, affairs leave Nvidia without its rockstar CEO
item.description: Jensen Huang, who built Nvidia into the world’s dominant AI chipmaker, is stepping down as CEO over extramarital affairs. DW examines how losing its figurehead will affect the firm and the US-China AI race.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: What are fossil fuels?
item.description: They are in our shampoo bottles, power our cars and heat our homes. But what actually are fossil fuels, and why do they matter?
item.dc:subject: Climate

item.title: Germany news: Police raid chapters of Gremium MC biker gang
item.description: Police in southwestern Germany launched major early-morning operations against a biker gang. The state of Baden-Württemberg is outlawing three of its chapters. Meanwhile, unions are planning more strikes.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Bundeswehr study exposes widespread sexual harassment in German military
item.description: Sexual misconduct in the Bundeswehr is far more widespread than previously known, with younger women disproportionately affected. Defense Minister Boris Pistorius has called for a policy of "zero tolerance."
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: Intelligent women get less help at work, study finds
item.description: Women who scored high on intelligence tests were seen as more hostile by their teammates and got less help, a new study finds. High-scoring men faced no such penalty. Research explains why.
item.dc:subject: Science

item.title: Fears of rising antisemitism in Europe
item.description: Holocaust survivor Regina Sluszny commemorates the victims of Auschwitz as Jewish communities across Europe face growing hostility. What does the promise of "Never Again" mean for Jewish life in Europe today?
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: Why the integration of immigrants in Germany remains a challenge
item.description: The Federal Office for Migration and Refugees has released a new Integration Report. It found that while the integration of people with a migrant background is improving, violent youth remain a problem.
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: Democracy study: One-quarter of Germans want a right-wing authoritarian dictatorship
item.description: The far-right AfD's electoral successes point to a new trend in Germany: Prejudice, resentment, and extremism are on the rise. A new study suggests satisfaction with democracy is at a low ebb.
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: Is AIIB's complaint mechanism failing affected communities?
item.description: The Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank has a grievance redress mechanism for people affected by projects it finances. But those seeking to file a complaint face significant hurdles. Critics say reforms are needed.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Wael Mohya could make German football history at 17
item.description: At just 17, Gladbach forward Wael Mohya has earned his first Germany call-up. The dual-national talent has chosen the DFB path for now — and could soon make modern national-team history.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: DW Science explainer on the default mode network: what your brain does when you aren't focusing on anything, and why it's important.
item.description: Doing nothing might be the ultimate brain hack. When you're bored, the brain goes into default mode network. It's not only healthy for you, but it may also shape the very essence of your identity.
item.dc:subject: Science

item.title: Germany slips in climate protection rankings as other countries make gains
item.description: Record renewable energy growth is driving climate progress in some countries, but Germany and many major emitters are falling behind.
item.dc:subject: Environment

item.title: British counterterrorism police arrest US soldier accused of spying on behalf of Russia
item.description: A member of the US Army has been arrested near Gloucester in England. Police said he was suspected of espionage activity in connection with Russia. Investigators from the US and UK are involved in the probe.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: UK Privy Council overrules Trinidad and Tobago gay sex law
item.description: A London court has overturned a Trinidad and Tobago law criminalizing consensual sexual relations between male same-sex couples. As a result of the colonial legacy, it is the independent country's last court of appeal.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Victims of Nazi war in Poland call on Germany for support
item.description: More than 80 years after the end of World War II, Polish victims of the Nazi regime are still waiting for a "humanitarian gesture" from Germany. The 2027 draft budget hasn't left them much hope for possible reparations.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Iran denies role in fridge hack, France summons ambassador
item.description: France has said it rules "nothing" out in response to a cyberattack on supermarket refrigeration units. Iran, however, said it categorically rejected Paris' "baseless and one-sided accusations" of IRGC involvement.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Controversial kinship: From colonial rule to the Holocaust?
item.description: Hitler once called Eastern Europe "Germany's India." A new exhibition examines the links between colonialism and Nazism, and the bitter debate over where comparisons illuminate history and where they fall short.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: Neuer injury gives Urbig chance to shape Bayern and Germany future
item.description: Manuel Neuer's latest injury gives Jonas Urbig a run of games in Bayern's goal. Marc-André ter Stegen remains Germany’s No. 1, but Urbig now has a chance to strengthen his case for the future.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Megaspeed and the battle to go high-end Nvidia chips into China
item.description: Jensen Huang's affair with a suspected Chinese spy has shone a light on Megaspeed, the company she worked for. It is under investigation in the US for smuggling Nvidia chips into China, which it denies.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Bulgaria highway pileup kills 12, dozens injured: PM
item.description: At least 12 people were killed and dozens injured in a series of crashes caused by thick fog in Bulgaria. Police, firefighters and paramedics were dispatched to the scene for the rescue operation.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Borussia Dortmund's Felix Nmecha and the question of religion
item.description: Felix Nmecha's "Crowns down" celebration has drawn criticism from a Borussia Dortmund fan club, reopening debate over faith, inclusion and religious messaging in football.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Fact check: Online disinformation rife after Krakow mass shooting
item.description: Fake and AI-manipulated images spread online in the hours after the Krakow attack, fueling false narratives about the mass shooting. DW Fact Check examined what's real, and what isn't.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Why electrification is the climate game changer we need
item.description: From EVs and electric buses on the road, heat pumps warming homes and solar panels powering appliances, the shift to electrifying tech is already in full swing. But what exactly does "electrification" mean?
item.dc:subject: Environment

item.title: Will Australia push for fossil fuel exit at UN talks?
item.description: The heat is on Australia as chief negotiator at the COP31 UN climate conference to forge a path away from coal and gas, and to protect Pacific neighbors facing rising sea levels.
item.dc:subject: Environment

item.title: US, Russia, Ukraine wrap up talks with prisoner exchange agreement
item.description: Peace talks between Russia, Ukraine and the US concluded in the United Arab Emirates. The two day talks were the first such meeting since February. DW has the latest updates.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Why malnutrition can go unnoticed, and what that means for our health
item.description: More than 2 billion people worldwide suffer from nutrient deficiencies, most of them in the Global South. The health consequences can be devastating.
item.dc:subject: Science

item.title: Iran war oil shock drives dip in global emissions, study shows
item.description: Global carbon emissions are expected to fall slightly in 2026, but not because of major progress on climate action. Instead, it's high energy prices following the US attack on Iran that's driving the trend.
item.dc:subject: Environment

item.title: New trilateral talks on Ukraine war in Abu Dhabi: What to expect?
item.description: Ukrainian and Russian representatives last met in February for talks on ending the war, but the same sticking points remain. Ukraine continues to demand security guarantees, which is a non-starter for Russia.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Russia: Independent Novaya Gazeta shuts its Moscow newsroom
item.description: The investigative newspaper is closing its doors after Russian authorities labeled it a "foreign agent" and ordered it vacate its Moscow premises.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Norway's ice hockey team says Russia replacing it at World Juniors
item.description: The wrangling over Russia's return to international ice hockey continues, with Norway saying it has been kicked out of the next major tournament to accommodate Russia. Switzerland has joined a "boycott."
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: 37 years after fall of Berlin Wall: How divided are Germans?
item.description: Three artists share their thoughts on the reunification of East and West Germany. How do they perceive a shared "we" and what gives them cause for optimism?
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: Germany: CDU names Ilse Aigner as candidate for president
item.description: The steering committtee of the CDU have announced Bavarian politician Ilse Aigner as presidential candidate. This gives her a good chance of becoming the first woman to occupy the role.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: EU aims to pick new ECB chief by year-end
item.description: Christine Lagarde's decision to step down early as head of the European Central Bank (ECB) has put the European Union on a tight schedule. The bloc expects to pick a new ECB chief by the end of December.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Why Nvidia CEO's affair with alleged Chinese spy matters for AI race
item.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has apologized for an affair with a woman the US believes was spying for China. The story could have profound implications for the world's most valuable company and the global AI race.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Who is Ilse Aigner, leading candidate for Germany's next president?
item.description: She would be the first female president and the first Christian Social Union politician to hold Germany's highest office. Ilse Aigner is the favored candidate for the Federal Convention vote on January 30.
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: Germany news: Germany marks fateful date of November 9
item.description: Germany is commemorating the Nazi-led November pogroms 88 years ago. Events are also being held to mark the anniversary of the fall of the Berlin Wall in 1989. DW has more.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Krakow mass shooting suspect has died in hospital, police in Poland say
item.description: The alleged gunman who killed six people in a shooting spree in the Polish city of Krakow has died of injuries sustained in a shootout with police, authorities say.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Germany: Chancellor Merz to nominate Aigner for president
item.description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz announced that he will nominate Ilse Aigner for federal president, paving the way for her to be the first woman to hold the office. DW has more.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: 'Never Again!': Holocaust remembrance under pressure
item.description: Only a few Holocaust survivors remain who can share their stories firsthand. Meanwhile, voices calling for an end to what they describe as a "cult of guilt" are growing louder. How can Holocaust remembrance survive?
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: As COP31 Antalya kicks off, can world move beyond big promises?
item.description: Droughts, floods and extreme heat are upping the pressure on delegates at the UN climate talks in Antalya, Turkey. Can countries move beyond pledges to concrete action?
item.dc:subject: Environment

item.title: Armenia's selective prosecution: A threat to EU relations?
item.description: While Brussels has refrained from harsh criticism, Armenian civil society has warned of selective justice against opposition figures. Could the EU's pragmatic stance risk repeating past mistakes?
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Should AI companies pay for the journalism they use?
item.description: Publishers say AI chatbots are using their reporting to answer readers' questions while sending back less traffic and less money. Should the companies that build these tools pay for the journalism they rely on?
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Germany hopes to host world ice hockey championship — without Russia
item.description: International protests continue after a court ruled that Russia must be allowed to return to international ice hockey. Germany is seeking a solution that will allow the country to host next year's world championship.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Amid protests, France's rising debt costs threaten stability
item.description: France plans to spend an extra €4 billion on education amid nationwide protests. But with public debt mounting and interest costs climbing, how much fiscal room does the government have?
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Ilse Aigner tipped by party allies as next German president
item.description: German media reports suggest that Bavarian politician Ilse Aigner's chances of becoming the next president are on the up. Long favored by her Bavarian CSU, now it seems Christian Democrats nationwide plan to back her.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Tesla to 'wind down' production of flop Cybertruck
item.description: Elon Musk's electric pickup for the future will start to be consigned to the past next year. The Cybertruck's bulk and crude shape meant it could only pass regulatory standards in more permissive markets.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: What to know about the IIHF Women's Ice Hockey World Championship
item.description: As ice hockey's governing body continues to wrangle over how to respond to a CAS order to reinstate Russia to international play, the top women's tournament gets underway in Denmark without Russia.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Exercise coaching boosts colon cancer survival
item.description: Evidence suggests exercise can keep more cancer patients alive. But what does "living longer" actually mean, and who does it apply to?
item.dc:subject: Science

item.title: European shares join a global sell-off as AI spending fears rattle Wall Street and Asian markets
item.description: European shares have fallen after sharp losses in Asia and on Wall Street. Doubts over huge AI investments and fears of curbs following the Democrats' US midterm victory have rattled global markets.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Germany’s Gen Z protests spark debate on integration, bias
item.description: Political debate about the recent Gen Z riots have raised the question: Can Germany talk about problems with integration without putting entire groups of people under suspicion?
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: Russia is back in world sport, but who is drug testing its athletes?
item.description: DW has found that three-quarters of Russia's weightlifting team had no independent out-of-competition testing before this year's world championships, despite the country's doping history.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Pioneering Jewish academy opens in Germany
item.description: A Jewish academy has opened its doors in Frankfurt. The Central Council of Jews in Germany, the country’s leading Jewish umbrella group, set up the project to combat hate and promote dialogue and learning nationally.
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: Cristiano Ronaldo announces retirement from international football
item.description: The announcement by the footballing legend comes just weeks after a public spat with Portugal coach Jorge Jesus over playing time.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: What the Democrats' midterms win means for the US economy and Trump
item.description: From high oil prices and data centers to tariffs and mounting debt, economic concerns played a key role in the crushing defeat of President Donald Trump's Republicans. So can the Democrats now make a difference?
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: The 2011 discovery of neo-Nazi killers aired biases in German policing
item.description: Many questions still surround the National Socialist Underground whose existence was revealed by neo-Nazi terrorist Beate Zschäpe on November 4, 2011. How has German society reacted to NSU crimes? Has justice been done?
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: Gold for the West Bank: Meet Palestinian karate champ Mariam Bsharat
item.description: The occupied West Bank is not an obvious breeding ground for sporting success. But Mariam Bsharat, 17, has beaten the odds to become a karate world champion and is making a new life in Germany.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Harry Potter films turns 25 ahead of new TV series' release
item.description: In 2001, "Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone" hit cinemas and took the world by storm. Today, anticipation for the new series is high, but its creator, J.K. Rowling, remains a controversial figure.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: Leading ice hockey nations, sponsors oppose Russia's return
item.description: Ice hockey's governing body says the impact of a court decision forcing it to reinstate Russia presents "significant practical and sporting challenges." Several leading nations say they won't play against Russian teams.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: BMW reports lower Q3 earnings as China woes mount
item.description: BMW reports a drop in profits in the July to September quarter amid fierce competition from China.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Germany's celebrated children's author Janosch has died
item.description: Bear, Tiger and Tiger-Duck: The author and illustrator Janosch achieved world fame with his heartwarming children's figures. He died at the age of 95.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: From rotten food to political opponents: Researchers explore how disgust relates to our beliefs, and why the connection is complicated
item.description: Some studies have linked disgust sensitivity to socially conservative attitudes. But does disgust shape our politics, or do our beliefs shape what we find disgusting?
item.dc:subject: Science

item.title: How Berlin's Arab queers are building their community
item.description: As the co-founder of the ADIRA Drag Festival, Lebanese performance artist, drag performer, DJ and cultural organizer Hassandra has become an essential part of Berlin's queer artistic landscape.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: Football: Spanish player dies on after cardiac arrest on the pitch
item.description: Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel has died following a collision with the opposing goalkeeper. The Spanish second-division club has said it is "heartbroken" by the loss.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Asian Cup postponed due to Middle East conflict
item.description: The Asian Cup has become the latest sporting event to be affected by the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. Organizers cite "exceptional circumstances" in Saudi Arabia, which has seen several Houthi attacks of late.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Could the AI boom make borrowing more expensive in Europe?
item.description: France, Germany and Italy face a volatile bond market as war inflation bites. With US tech giants now issuing billions in AI bonds, they are competing with cash-strapped European governments.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Germany news: Ukraine in focus at Berlin Security Conference
item.description: A security conference in the German capital is addressing defending Europe against threats from Russia. Meanwhile, Germany's justice minister wants to raise penalties for sexual offenses. DW has more.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Ice hockey officials considering options after CAS order to reinstate Russia
item.description: Ice hockey's ruling body is deciding how to respond to a decision by the Court of Arbitration for Sport that allows Russia back into international competition. Germany hasn't ruled out pulling out as a tournament host.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: LA communities kick out Big Oil
item.description: After years of advocacy from residents and legal battles with Big Oil, Los Angeles voted to ban drilling and phase out oil extraction in the city. It's the first city in the United States to kick the oil industry out.
item.dc:subject: Environment

item.title: Merz says next German president 'must be a woman' — report
item.description: German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier's second term is due to end in March next year. Meanwhile, Merz has called for 'digital sovereignty' in the era of AI.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Kimi Antonelli makes history as youngest F1 champion
item.description: Kimi Antonelli became Formula One's youngest world champion and Italy's first since 1953 when he finished third in Sunday's thrilling and crash-hit Mexico City Grand Prix.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Ethnic Germans in Kazakhstan face legacy of the Soviet Union
item.description: Kazakhstan is struggling to deal with the legacy of the Soviet dictatorship. Some 85 years ago, Stalin deported hundreds of thousands of people: Some 400,000 ethnic Germans living in the USSR were sent to Kazakhstan.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Embarrassing name? How we live with names we don't like
item.description: What happens when your name evokes laughter or ridicule? Research points to negative life outcomes, but some people learn to embrace unfortunate names.
item.dc:subject: Science

item.title: Germany news: Merz hopes for Korean reunification at DMZ
item.description: Chancellor Friedrich Merz has expressed hope for Korean reunification during a visit to the heavily fortified border. Meanwhile, President Steinmeier has held talks with China's Xi Jinping in Beijing.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Bayern Munich's Kenya friendly highlights Africa's growing pull for global sport
item.description: Bayern Munich are to open Nairobi's new Raila Odinga International Stadium against Ajax as Kenya prepares for AFCON 2027. The match highlights Africa's growing sports ambitions — and questions over cost and legacy.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: IIHF ordered to allow Russia back into world championships
item.description: The Court of Arbitration for Sport has ruled that Russian teams must be allowed to take part in international ice hockey tournaments. The IIHF had banned Russia following the country's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: The dachshund, a humorous icon with political symbolism
item.description: From Picasso to Andy Warhol, a surprising number of artists have portrayed the German breed. But the dachshund has also at times been co-opted as a political symbol.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: Germany's Alexander Zverev clinches tennis No. 1 ranking
item.description: Alexander Zverev is the second German man, after Boris Becker, to clinch the No. 1 spot in tennis.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: 'Star Trek' star Patrick Stewart dies age 86
item.description: The Shakespearean actor landed the role of a lifetime as "Star Trek" Captain Picard. He passed away at age 86.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: India increases growth forecast for fiscal year
item.description: India's Ministry of Finance has increased its growth forecasts for the current fiscal year. But it also warned about inflation, particularly for fuel and energy, amid continued instability in the Middle East.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Volkswagen logs Q3 operating loss of €5.86 billion on Porsche writedown
item.description: The Volkswagen Group has filed its worst quarterly performance since the height of the "Dieselgate" scandal in 2015. Share prices climbed in response, however, perhaps because the bad news was so well signposted.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Russia shadow fleet sanctions: Can the EU act without US?
item.description: The US is reportedly considering ways to convert "dark tankers" into legitimate vessels, allowing them to transport crude oil that is not subject to sanctions.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany's health scare highlights the need for better support for elite coaches
item.description: Vincent Kompany’s health concern is a reminder that elite football's pressures affect coaches too. Better support, clearer structures and mental health safeguards are increasingly vital.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Can we regrow damaged seagrass meadows?
item.description: Seagrass protects coasts, shelters thousands of species and stores CO2. But some 30% of this valuable ecosystem has disappeared since the late 19th century. Can we bring it back?
item.dc:subject: Environment

item.title: EU's 'Made in Europe' push unnerves global auto suppliers
item.description: In shielding Europe's carmakers from Chinese rivals, the EU risks hurting close partners from Turkey and Morocco to Japan and South Korea. Billions in trade and hundreds of thousands of European jobs are at stake.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Africa's first Youth Olympics open in Senegal amid hope and scrutiny
item.description: Senegal is hosting Africa's first Youth Olympics, with 2,700 young athletes competing in Dakar, Diamniadio and Saly. The Games bring pride and hope, but also questions over cost, rights and legacy.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Harry Kane: Ballon d’Or for Bayern Munich striker
item.description: Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane has won football's most prestigious individual prize, beating Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal. Kane has developed even more in the Bundesliga despite an uneven league.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: What Germany thinks of carmaker Audi's $4 billion deal with Trump
item.description: The luxury carmaker is set to open its first factory in the United States — a move Trump credits to his tariffs. DW examines the German reaction amid a massive auto industry cull at home.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: EU moves to loosen rules on pesticide use as experts sound the alarm
item.description: The European Union wants to relax rules for pesticides, saying it will be easier for farmers to adopt more environmentally friendly options. But health and environmental experts say the risks are far too great.
item.dc:subject: Environment

item.title: Can Germany revive its economy before the far-right AfD gains ground?
item.description: Conflicts, rising costs and Chinese competition are testing Germany's economic model like never before. Can new growth sectors create jobs and ease voters' economic fears, thereby helping contain the far-right AfD?
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: US sanctions target Iran's rail sector as Tehran shifts cargo from sea routes to overland corridors
item.description: As US sanctions expand to Iran's rail sector, Tehran is relying more heavily on overland links with China and Central Asia. But capacity constraints, delays and costs limit rail's ability to replace maritime trade.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Rising emissions and temperatures: The cost of Trump's climate retreat is now clear
item.description: The world is set to breach the critical 1.5-degree temperature limit, with Donald Trump's US withdrawal from climate action worsening the outlook, according to a UN report. But there is a small silver lining.
item.dc:subject: Climate

item.title: Why US investors are snapping up Germany's famed Mittelstand
item.description: Increasing amounts of US capital are flowing into Germany's traditional industrial firms and family-owned businesses. As many business owners struggle to find successors, more companies are becoming acquisition targets.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Brutal, revolutionary empire builder: Genghis Khan's legacy
item.description: Berlin is host to a major exhibition on the founder of the Mongol Empire and his successors. Here's how Genghis Khan disrupted the course of history.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: The homeless man living in front of a London mega-mansion
item.description: Anders Fernstedt lives in London without any money. The Swedish native has built a most unusual home under the porch of a house worth over €200 million. How did that happen?
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: China's influence in the gaming industry is growing
item.description: Home to more than 700 million gamers, China is the world's largest gaming market — but it's also one of the most tightly regulated. The effects reach far beyond China, impacting players around the world.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Who was Eva Mamlok? Berlin square renamed after Jewish anti-fascist resistance fighter
item.description: She started taking action against Hitler as a teenager and never stopped until her death in a concentration camp. Berlin's Blücherplatz is now being renamed after her.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: EU promotes sovereign, trusted AI as it struggles to catch US and China
item.description: At an international AI summit in Dublin, EU leaders promoted trusted and independent artificial intelligence. Critics question whether the bloc can close the gap with the US and China while maintaining strict regulation.
